source_version: Capella (continuously deployed, no discrete version number)

concepts.label: Bucket (Capella data container)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - no existing concept in the registry covers Capella's bucket/scope/collection data-container hierarchy; this page is its overview

concepts.label: Couchbase Server 7.6
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - server-version-string anomaly (known recurring pattern), no existing version:server-7-6 concept in the registry

concepts.label: _system scope
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a special, read-only, non-deletable scope automatically added to buckets, distinct from the general capella:scope concept

relations.subject: capella:scope
relations.evidence: A scope is a data container that exists inside a Capella bucket. Use scopes to group related [collections](#collections).

relations.subject: capella:system-scope
relations.evidence: The `_system` scope is part of all clusters using Couchbase Server 7.6 or later. When you upgrade a cluster to Couchbase Server 7.6, Capella adds the `_system` scope to your existing buckets.

notable_absence.finding: This is a pure concept/overview page (no procedures) and cites no capella-role:* gate at all - role requirements are deferred entirely to manage-buckets.md and scopes-collections.md ('For more information about how to create a new bucket, see Create a Bucket'). No Enterprise/Community edition badges and no server-version-string citations of the KNOWN recurring kind - but note the `_system` scope note DOES cite a specific server version ('Couchbase Server 7.6 or later'), which is the server-version-string anomaly recurring yet again, just in a slightly different context (a scope's existence gated by server version, not a statement's syntax).

cross_component_finding: This page's data-container hierarchy (bucket > scope > collection) has never been modeled in the registry before, despite the n1ql/ batch's CREATE BUCKET/SCOPE/COLLECTION statement pages implicitly assuming it. The `_system` scope (containing read-only `_mobile` and `_query` collections) and the `_default` scope/collection auto-creation behavior are Capella-specific structural facts with no privilege or role gating mentioned on this page at all - access control for buckets/scopes/collections is documented on the sibling procedure pages, not here.
cross_product_finding: The bucket-type/storage-backend distinction (Couchstore vs. Magma) reuses the exact same storage-engine:* concepts already promoted from the reference/n1ql batches - this page adds no new storage-engine vocabulary, just a Capella-specific compaction/purge-scheduling behavioral layer on top (30%/50% fragmentation thresholds, 3-day tombstone purge, 60-day App-Service-linked tombstone retention) that server/'s own docs don't describe in these exact terms.
